> Viral Claims Online
  
> Following reports of the deployment, some social media users suggested the move meant the United States was preparing for a ground invasion of Iran. One account on the platform X wrote: "The Pentagon just approved deploying boots on the ground in Iran with an Expeditionary Unit of 2,500 Marines."
  
> 
  
> Another post claimed: "The Pentagon is preparing for the possibility of a ground invasion in Iran, moving a Marine Expeditionary Unit toward the Middle East as Trump’s war grows out of control."
  
> 
  
> However, officials say the deployment does not indicate that US forces are preparing for a ground invasion.
  
> 
  
> What is Actually Being Deployed?
  
> Reports say the unit being sent to the region is the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit. The unit is normally based in Japan and usually operates under the United States Indo-Pacific Command. It has now been redirected toward the Middle East.
  
> 
  
> Officials say such units provide a wide range of military capabilities that commanders can use if required, rather than being designed solely for ground combat operations.
  
> 
  
> The unit includes advanced aircraft, including a squadron of F-35 Lightning II fighter jets and a squadron of Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey aircraft capable of supporting various missions.
  
> 
  
> Purpose of the Deployment
  
> According to The Wall Street Journal, the move is intended to help respond to Iran’s attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has said it wants to disrupt oil tanker traffic passing through the waterway, which is one of the world’s most important routes for energy supplies.
  
> 
  
> An amphibious ready group typically includes several naval vessels, such as an assault ship, two transport dock ships and a support vessel carrying Marines and equipment.
  
> 
  
> Officials say the deployment is aimed at strengthening US military resources in the region, giving commanders additional options if the situation escalates.

I sat down, thought about it, read about it, talked about it, and my very own conclusion is that the CCP is NOT the good guy in the story. And just fyi, I criticize the US government a lot more than I do the CCP. But fundamentally, at the root of each system is a different idea, and I prefer the American one, with all its faults, to the Chinese one, with all its faults. You’re welcome to disagree, but for either of these two governments and systems to try and position themselves opposite the other is just ridiculous 😅😅 am I defending the US government? No. But does the CCP have a good record with universities and intellectuals? NO!

On the nuclear concern, it is understandable to feel anxious, but a direct nuclear exchange between major powers remains extremely unlikely because of mutually assured destruction. Leaders sometimes use dramatic rhetoric, but actually launching nukes would be a civilization altering move that carries consequences no rational actor can ignore. So while the situation could be tense and unpredictable, jumping straight to “we’d all need to get out asap” assumes the most extreme outcome rather than the most probable one.
